title: Rav Menashe bar Yirmeyah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Pesachim 28a and [Nazir 65b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.65b.3) for “Menashe bar Yirmeyah said in the name of Rav.” He also cites Bava Batra 146a (compare [Bava Batra 147a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.147a.8-9)), where Rav Menashia bar Yirmeyah says, “From here,” and then Rami bar Yechezkel says, “From here.” Hyman infers that Menashe was a student of Rav.

[Ohr Zarua II 84:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Ohr_Zarua%2C_Volume_II.84.1) (Hyman’s locator: ספ״ד) cites “Chanan bar Immi said before Rav Yehudah in Menashe bar Yirmeyah’s name.” Hyman traces this to [Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.6.5.2), where he says an error occurred: “Anan bar R’ Ima [supplied אנן בר׳ אימא] said before Rabbi Yehudah: Menashya bar Menashe Yirmeyah, provided…” Hyman says it SHOULD READ as cited in Ohr Zarua, and identifies him as Rav Menashya bar Yirmeyah, Rav’s student.[^1]

notes.text: [Hyman, vol. III, p. 895](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/b/ba/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._III._1910.pdf#page=62) gives Pesachim 28a and Bava Batra 146a. The consecutive proofs are at Bava Batra 147a. The attribution to Menashya is explicit in Nazir; the same name was not located in the checked Pesachim passages. The consulted Yerushalmi reads Anan ke-Rabbi Immi and gives the longer chain, while Ohr Zarua has Chanan bar Immi and the shorter Menashe form. Hyman uses the latter to correct the former. Compare [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2522&lang=en) for the citation history.
